  "markdown_report": "Select **joint lexical-residual HSTU** as the first experiment. At 10% research progress, preserve the supplied backbone and objective while testing one representation change. No improvement has been measured; objective and temporal alternatives remain separate experiments.

**Insights from the starting point and diagnosis**

1. Item IDs do not explicitly share lexical evidence across products. Scratch token learning could transfer functional distinctions, provided tokenization preserves identifiers, units, and negators; mean pooling nevertheless loses word order.
2. Users reject broad relevance and recommendations disconnected from recent narrow interests. Richer representations of recent interactions target both failures, but cannot establish current purpose, satisfied needs, compatibility, or psychological intent.
3. Electronics and Industrial show sampled training-pair error rates of 10.38% and 8.22%, versus 0.14% and 0.36% for Movies and CDs. This motivates testing discrimination, without identifying its cause or establishing validation weakness.
4. Final-item removal reduces training-prefix hit10 by 0.375 for Movies and CDs; corresponding intervals include zero for Industrial and Electronics. Preserve existing recent-history signals; alignment scores of 0.5073–0.5212 indicate near-zero mean cosine, not representation collapse or recommendation diversity.

**Insights from related work**

1. [HSTU-BLaIR](https://kdd2025llm4ecommerce.github.io/assets/accepted/13_HSTU_BLaIR_Lightweight_Cont.pdf) motivates text augmentation, but its pretrained encoder is prohibited. Its gains do not establish benefits from scratch tokens.
2. [Semantic fusion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18166) motivates accounting for ID/text differences. [TensorFlow Recommenders](https://www.tensorflow.org/recommenders/examples/featurization) supplies a scratch title-pooling precedent, although retrieval evidence does not validate this sequential residual design.
3. [Hard-BPR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19276) motivates bounded hard-negative influence; [HSTU](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17152) motivates temporal alternatives. Neither establishes that these changes address the observed failures.
4. [Sampled-metric analysis](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) limits conclusions to the pinned candidate protocol. [Selection-bias analysis](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html) explains why repeated validation selection makes winning scores optimistic.

**Framework and candidate assessment**

Directions target representation specificity, ranking discrimination, and temporal relevance. Scores are prospective judgments: O/P/U/M/D denote originality, potential, user alignment, model alignment, and difficulty; higher D means harder implementation.

| Atomic idea | O/P/U/M/D | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lexical residual | 3/7/7/7/5 | Feasible transfer of specific functional evidence; directly tests representation quality | Fusion is established; sparse tokens and superficial lexical shortcuts may dominate |
| Warm-start bounded hard-negative loss | 4/7/5/8/5 | Targets difficult ranking pairs with false-negative safeguards | Does not directly encode compatibility or changing purpose; mining adds cost |
| Relative elapsed-time bias | 3/7/8/5/6 | Could distinguish persistent interests from transient activity | Diagnostics do not identify missing temporal information as the cause |
| Parameter-matched local CNN text residual | 3/6/7/6/6 | Tests whether local phrase order helps functional distinctions | More computation and tuning; no supplied recommendation evidence establishes superiority |

**Selected algorithm**

Pool jointly trained title and description tokens separately, project into ID space, and add a scale-matched residual with a bounded scale initialized to 0.05. Missing text contributes exactly zero. Share the effective embedding across histories and candidate scoring; retain corrected causal HSTU and its baseline loss.

This explicitly targets broad matches lacking specific function and recommendations insufficiently connected to recent narrow interests. The model-facing hypothesis is improved sampled pair discrimination in Electronics and Industrial. Duplicate functionality and satisfied needs remain unresolved hypotheses, and lexical overlap may amplify those failures.

Fix a deterministic 10,000-token vocabulary, 32-dimensional token embeddings, 16-token titles, and 64-token descriptions; preserve alphanumeric identifiers and negators. Record OOV, missingness, and truncation rates. Compute valid-row normalization in FP32 with epsilon 1e-3 and nonzero projection initialization. Isolate added-module RNG use and verify unchanged baseline initialization and subsequent RNG states.

Train one model per category with unchanged seeds, routing, splits, objective, and training limits. Preserve final-nonpadding readout, serialize all lexical assets with the checkpoint, update the predictor writer, and retain diagnostic interfaces using effective embeddings.

Prespecify the baseline and first lexical configuration before training; log every configuration and epoch comparison, retaining the supplied checkpoint rule. Additional no-text, title-only, globally shuffled, and frequency/length/missingness-matched shuffled-text retraining controls require budget allocation and each uses one model per category. Identifier/boilerplate masking probes shortcuts; inference corruption is only a sensitivity check. Report paired gains by training-frequency and text-availability bins, plus popularity and coverage; these do not prove semantic causality.

Select solely by pinned macro validation HR@10. With identical users, candidates, and ties, report paired gains/losses, exact per-category McNemar tests, and a paired-user bootstrap averaging categories equally. One changed hit equals 0.5 category percentage points or 0.125 macro points. Intervals condition on fixed candidates, datasets, and seed; winner-only intervals do not correct adaptive selection. Label results exploratory, with no full-catalog or held-out improvement claim.",

Prespecify the baseline and first lexical configuration, retain the supplied epoch-selection rule, log every epoch/configuration comparison, and use a descriptive practical-effect threshold of +0.5 macro percentage points without replacing the host selection metric. All training and controls consume the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Additional matched retraining controls are alternatives scheduled within remaining budget: no text, title-only residual, intact title-plus-description, global item-text shuffling, frequency-bin shuffling with matched text length/missingness, and a parameter-matched local CNN. Each control has one independently trained model per category and never combines predictions. Token shuffling does not diagnose order dependence in an unordered mean encoder. Identifier and boilerplate masking test lexical shortcuts; inference-only corruption introduces distribution shift. Report paired results by train-only item-frequency bins and text availability, plus recommendation popularity and catalog coverage under explicitly stated candidate protocols. Persistence under matched shuffling weakens semantic attribution; intact-text tail gains support, but do not prove, semantic benefit.

Select exclusively by the pinned validation macro HR@10: 200 users/category, 99 unique negatives, evaluator seed 42, identical users/candidates/tie handling. Where host per-user outcomes are available, compute paired hit differences, gains/losses, exact two-sided McNemar tests per category, and a paired-user bootstrap independently within categories, averaging the four differences equally. Use 10,000 bootstrap replicates with a local seed 42 and report percentile 95% intervals. One changed hit gives 0.5 category percentage points and 0.125 macro points. These intervals exclude training and negative-sampling variability and do not correct adaptive winner selection; label all search findings exploratory. Do not substitute the 1,000-candidate training-prefix diagnostic for validation or claim full-catalog performance.     "pseudocode": "# Integration pseudocode: preserve the supplied HSTU and training loop.
# Construct and initialize the entire baseline first, in its original order.
baseline = construct_corrected_baseline()
baseline_reference_parameters = snapshot_for_initialization_check(baseline)
with torch.random.fork_rng(devices=touched_cuda_devices):
    torch.manual_seed(42)
    lexical = LexicalResidualEmbedding(
        identity=baseline.item_emb,
        token_dim=32, vocab_size=10000,
        title_limit=16, description_limit=64,
        initial_scale=0.05, eps=1e-3,
    )
# The wrapper must not reinitialize identity or any existing baseline module.
# Verify original parameter equality and RNG-state restoration.
baseline.item_emb = lexical

class LexicalResidualEmbedding(nn.Module):
    def forward(self, ids):
        identity = self.id_embedding(ids)
        flat_ids = ids.reshape(-1)
        flat_identity = identity.reshape(-1, identity.shape[-1])
        valid = flat_ids.ne(0) & self.text_present[flat_ids]
        rows = valid.nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
        residual = torch.zeros_like(flat_identity, dtype=torch.float32)
        with torch.autocast(device_type=identity.device.type, enabled=False):
            if rows.numel() > 0:
                selected = flat_ids[rows]
                # masked_mean divides by max(valid-token count, 1).
                title = masked_mean(
                    self.tokens(self.title_ids[selected]).float(),
                    self.title_mask[selected],
                )
                description = masked_mean(
                    self.tokens(self.description_ids[selected]).float(),
                    self.description_mask[selected],
                )
                pooled = torch.cat([title, description], dim=-1)
                text = F.linear(pooled, self.projection.weight.float(), bias=None)
                direction = text / text.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-3)
                magnitude = flat_identity[rows].float().norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True).detach()
                values = torch.sigmoid(self.scale_logit.float()) * magnitude * direction
                residual = residual.index_copy(0, rows, values)
            effective = flat_identity.float() + residual
            effective = effective * flat_ids.ne(0).unsqueeze(-1)
        return effective.reshape(identity.shape).to(identity.dtype)

# Unchanged causal HSTU training: no detached embedding cache.
features = model.log2feats(sequence)
positive_scores = model.predict_score(features, positive)
negative_scores = model.predict_score(features, negative)
loss = unchanged_baseline_loss(positive_scores, negative_scores, positive.ne(0))
optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
loss.backward()
apply_baseline_gradient_clipping_if_configured(model)
optimizer.step()

# Left-padding-safe inference readout.
positions = torch.arange(sequence.shape[1], device=sequence.device)
last = torch.where(sequence.ne(0), positions, -1).amax(dim=1)
valid_rows = last.ge(0)
readout = features[valid_rows, last[valid_rows]]
# Handle empty rows with the supplied baseline policy.

# Save exactly one selected checkpoint/category, including all lexical assets.
# Predictor writer reconstructs the same class, loads strictly, and calls eval().
# Host evaluation is unchanged; paired analysis uses its exposed user outcomes.
for category in FOUR_CATEGORIES:
    differences[category] = hit_new[category] - hit_baseline[category]
    gains = count(differences[category] == 1)
    losses = count(differences[category] == -1)
    p_value = exact_two_sided_binomial_test(gains, gains + losses, p=0.5)
    # If there are no discordant users, report p=1.
# Bootstrap paired users separately within each category, average category
# differences equally, and label intervals conditional and exploratory.",
